title: A First Test Post: First Variation of Area
text:
This is a sample mathematical post. It is mainly used to test display math, theorem environments, and proof blocks.
Let \(\Sigma^2 \subset M^3\) be a closed two-sided surface with unit normal \(\nu\). If the variation vector field is \(X=f\nu\), then the first variation of area is
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0} \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma_t)
= -\int_\Sigma H f \, d\mu .
\tag{1}\]

Theorem 1 (Minimal surfaces as critical points) A closed two-sided surface \(\Sigma \subset M\) is minimal if and only if it is a critical point of the area functional under all compactly supported normal variations.


Proof. By Equation 1, the first variation vanishes for every smooth function \(f\) if and only if
\[
\int_\Sigma H f\,d\mu = 0
\]
for all \(f\). This is equivalent to \(H=0\) on \(\Sigma\).

The statement above is Theorem 1. In future posts, this style can be used for lemmas, propositions, definitions, remarks, and equations.

Remark 1 (Writing style). For a research note, I usually want three layers: the formal statement, the geometric meaning, and the proof mechanism.

title: About
text:
I use this website as a public mathematical notebook. The main purpose is not to make finished survey articles, but to record ideas clearly enough that they remain useful months later.
The guiding style is simple: state the result, explain the geometric picture, then write the proof in a form that can be checked.
